name: British uniform penny post
description: A domestic postal tariff made prepaid letters within a weight limit cost the same regardless of distance.

impact.note: Cheap prepaid uniform postage multiplied letter-writing and was copied by many countries; an existing service reorganised, with stamps and postal unions as successors.

date.label: 10 January 1840
date.basis: Date or stated historical interval in cited source; see caveats.

events.statement: The British postal service introduced a uniform penny rate for eligible prepaid inland letters.

contributions.resource: Advocated and oversaw implementation of the reform.

evidence.supports: Museum dates uniform penny post to 10 January 1840 and explains weight-based distance-independent rates.

events.caveats: One penny applied to prepaid letters within the weight limit, not every item; unpaid letters cost more. Adhesive stamps were not yet available.

measures.subject: Inland prepaid letter up to half an ounce
measures.conditions: Nominal pre-decimal British penny; prepaid; heavier and unpaid letters cost more.

evidence.supports: The later 1840 Act states one penny for prepaid inland letters not exceeding half an ounce, with a higher charge if unpaid.

measures.subject: British chargeable postal letters in 1850
measures.conditions: Approximately; museum says almost 350 million. Counts letters, not users.

evidence.supports: Reports almost 350 million chargeable letters by 1850.

caveats: The reform did not invent postal services, and means of payment, weight limits and eligibility matter.

research.note: Initial sourced research; independent review pending. Independent review distinguishes issued-for-use from first sale and checks statutory half-ounce and unpaid rates; 1850 volume counts letters, not senders.
